headline: SK hynix overtakes Samsung as South Korea's most valuable company for first time since 2000
summary: SK hynix shares surged 5.6% to lift its market capitalization to $1.35 trillion, surpassing Samsung's valuation for the first time in over two decades.
details: SK hynix has become South Korea's most valuable listed company, unseating Samsung Electronics for the first time since November 2000. The memory giant's shares closed up 5.6% on Monday, pushing its market capitalization to 2,080.4 trillion won ($1.35 trillion).

This milestone is attributed to a rally of over 340% this year, driven almost entirely by demand for High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) supplied to AI chipmakers like Nvidia. SK hynix currently holds a dominant 61% of the global HBM market for 2025, compared to Samsung's 17% and Micron's 21%.

Investors are favoring SK hynix's focus on pure-play memory, particularly HBM, which offers higher margins and ties suppliers to specific AI accelerators. This contrasts with Samsung's diversified business, which spans smartphones, displays, and home appliances.

SK hynix's strategic investment in HBM throughout the 2023 downturn, despite a significant operating loss, has paid off. Samsung reportedly faced yield and qualification delays with its HBM3E chips, slowing down major orders from Nvidia.

While Samsung disputes the ranking by including preferred shares, which would raise its valuation, the current gap highlights the immense demand and profitability of HBM technology. Both companies, along with Micron, have passed HBM4 certification, indicating continued competition in next-generation memory.

SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won's long-term vision to transform Hynix from a commodity memory producer into an indispensable semiconductor company appears to be materializing, underscoring the strategic importance of AI-driven memory solutions.

SK hynix has officially surpassed Samsung Electronics as South Korea's most valuable company, marking the first time since 2000.

SK hynix has become South Korea's most valuable listed company, unseating Samsung Electronics for the first time since November 2000. The memory giant's shares closed up 5.6% on Monday, pushing its market capitalization to 2,080.4 trillion won ($1.35 trillion).

Investors are favoring SK hynix's focus on pure-play memory, particularly HBM, which offers higher margins and ties suppliers to specific AI accelerators. This contrasts with Samsung's diversified business, which spans smartphones, displays, and home appliances.

SK hynix's strategic investment in HBM throughout the 2023 downturn, despite a significant operating loss, has paid off. Samsung reportedly faced yield and qualification delays with its HBM3E chips, slowing down major orders from Nvidia.

While Samsung disputes the ranking by including preferred shares, which would raise its valuation, the current gap highlights the immense demand and profitability of HBM technology. Both companies, along with Micron, have passed HBM4 certification, indicating continued competition in next-generation memory.

SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won's long-term vision to transform Hynix from a commodity memory producer into an indispensable semiconductor company appears to be materializing, underscoring the strategic importance of AI-driven memory solutions.
